title: Cross-protocol degradation canary and contract harness for streaming & tool-calls
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a lightweight, automated canary and contract-harness that continuously detects protocol-level regressions and functional degradations across streaming APIs, tool/function calling, and structured-output semantics. This ticket scopes the cross-protocol detection harness (server+client probes), CI gate integration, golden prompt sentinel set, and alerting/rollback playbook.

Why: recent incidents show subtle semantic drift when model runtime changes or when shims between protocol versions are applied (partial JSON fragments mid-stream, interleaved toolcall tokens, and mismatched event boundaries). Existing regression suites catch many failures but miss low-amplitude behavioral degradations that surface in production under multiplexed streaming. The harness will provide an always-on signal in CI and staging to block releases that introduce cross-protocol regressions.

Scope:
- Design and implement a probe runner that emits a diverse set of golden prompts and multiplexed tool-call scenarios to hosted and dedicated endpoints across protocol versions (v1 streaming, v1.1 multiplex, and SDK shims).
- Detect both contract violations (missing required event type, malformed JSON chunk) and behavioral degradation (percent change in canonical token sequence, divergence in toolcall invocation ordering).
- Integrate with CI: nightly regressions + PR-level smoke checks for critical paths.
- Canary automation: automated canary runs during blue-green / canary deploys with thresholds to auto-fail rollout and trigger rollback.
- Observability: per-probe fingerprints, delta metrics, and synthetic traces pushed to Console dashboards and incident channel.

Out of scope: full model-behavior testing (evaluations that depend on model weights) and exhaustive golden corpus expansion - those are separate projects.
acceptance_criteria: Probe runner executes nightly against hosted and dedicated endpoints and produces a deterministic report artifact
CI pipeline includes a PR smoke job that runs a reduced probe set and fails on contract violations
Canary automation runs post-deploy and triggers rollback when contract-violation rate > 0.5% or behavioral-divergence score exceeds threshold
Console dashboard shows per-probe fingerprints, and alerts route to #platform-api-incidents with runbook link
At least three representative golden prompts covering streaming + interleaved tool-calls and structured JSON partials are included and versioned
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after postmortem for incident INV-2026-02 where a runtime patch caused truncated NDJSON chunks in multiplexed streams. Tagged ENG owners for API Conformance project.

2026-02-18 Miguel Ortega: Scoped probe architecture w/ sidecar approach. Decision: run probes as an independent job that can target multiple protocol endpoints and collect raw wire traces + parsed events. Will reuse existing golden-prompt corpus but add multiplexed tool-call scenarios.

2026-02-25 Design review (Samir Chen): Reviewed probe signal design. Recommendation: two-tier detection - contract assertions (hard fail) and divergence scoring (soft fail). Use lightweight fingerprints (token-level edit distance + event boundary mismatch count).

2026-03-02 Eng update (Miguel Ortega): PoC runner implemented in runtime/testbed/probes. PoC covers streaming v1 -> v1.1 and SDK shim. Found a regression where SDK shim emitted duplicate TOOL_CALL_START events under backpressure. Filing follow-up ENG-88145 to fix shim state machine.

2026-03-05 QA (Priya Das): Added three golden prompts focused on partial JSON emissions and interleaved toolcalls. Verified parity across dedicated and hosted in staging. Added acceptance criteria to require dashboard visibility.

2026-03-09 CI (Miguel Ortega): Opened PRs to add a reduced smoke probe to PR pipeline and a nightly full-run job. PRs: runtime#4282 and ci-config#117. Noted flakiness on low-memory nodes; gating those nodes out for PR smoke until we tune timeouts.
test_plan: 1) Nightly full-run: run the golden corpus (N=120 prompts) against hosted, dedicated, and SDK-shim endpoints; collect raw traces; compute contract-violation counts and divergence scores. 2) PR smoke: run reduced set (N=8) that covers canonical streaming-toolcall interleaving cases. 3) Canary: run reduced set during rollout at 0%, 5%, 25%, 100% traffic steps; abort rollout when hard-fail or metric thresholds met. 4) Post-failure: auto-collect artifacts (trace + parsed events + token diffs) into artifacts storage and open an incident with link.
runbook: If probe run reports a hard contract violation: 1) Immediately mark canary failed and trigger automated rollback. 2) Open incident, include raw trace and failing prompt. 3) On-call inspects token-level diff and event boundary mismatch count to triage between runtime regression vs shim mismatch. 4) If false positive suspected, run targeted replay with increased timeout and verify. 5) Escalate to runtime-team lead if regression verified.
